The vision of a Sashakt Bharat is being redefined. As geopolitical shifts, 
supply chain disruptions, technological breakthroughs and evolving energy 
dynamics continue to reshape the global landscape, national strength can 
no longer be measured solely by economic growth or resource availability. 
It is increasingly shaped by resilience, adaptability and the capability  to 
anticipate change. As India advances towards its long-term development 
ambitions, the need is not merely to build a stronger nation, but to reimagine 
what strength itself means in an era of unprecedented transformation.
For India, this reimagined vision lies in building resilient infrastructure, 
securing critical resources, fostering innovation, accelerating industrial 
capabilities and building institutions that can thrive amid uncertainty. 
The aim is  enhancing self-reliance while remaining globally connected, 
expanding opportunities while safeguarding stability, and shaping the 
foundations necessary to support the aspirations of a rapidly growing 
economy and society.
Reimagining 
Sashakt 
Against this backdrop, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) 
continues to play a pivotal role in enabling national progress. As the energy 
landscape undergoes significant change, the Company is strengthening 
its core business, expanding its capabilities and pursuing new avenues of 
growth to enhance long-term competitiveness. Through investments in 
capacity, diversification, technology and operational excellence, HPCL is 
preparing itself to address emerging opportunities while contributing to 
India’s evolving development priorities.
The theme, “Reimagining Sashakt Bharat” reflects this broader 
vision of nation-building. It embodies a commitment to looking beyond 
conventional definitions of growth and embracing new possibilities that 
strengthen economic resilience, energy preparedness and future readiness. 
As India embarks on its next phase of development,, HPCL remains focused 
on supporting a nation that is not only stronger today, but better equipped 
for the opportunities and complexities of the future.

ABOUT THE REPORT
This Integrated Annual Report marks Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited’s (HPCL) third Integrated 
Report and presents a holistic overview of the company’s strategy, operational performance and value creation 
journey during FY 2025–26. The Report highlights how HPCL continues to strengthen its core businesses while 
advancing towards a more resilient, diversified and future-ready energy portfolio in a rapidly evolving global 
energy landscape. It provides insights into HPCL’s approach towards sustainable growth, operational excellence, 
stakeholder engagement and long-term value creation across financial and non-financial capitals.
The statutory and financial information presented in this Report has been prepared in accordance with 
the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules framed thereunder, the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and the applicable 
Secretarial Standards.

The Company has established a strong presence across the 
entire downstream energy value chain, encompassing refining, 
petroleum marketing, LPG, lubricants, aviation fuels, pipelines, 
natural gas, and emerging clean energy businesses. Through 
an extensive nationwide infrastructure network, HPCL delivers 
reliable, safe, and sustainable energy solutions to millions of 
customers across India.
As India’s leading marketer of industrial and automotive 
lubricants, HPCL continues to diversify its energy portfolio 
through investments in natural gas, biofuels, green hydrogen, 
electric mobility, and renewable energy. Guided by its Net 
Zero 2040 commitment, the Company is driving innovation, 
operational excellence, and sustainable growth while supporting 
India’s energy security and low-carbon transition.

HPCL offers a comprehensive portfolio of energy products and solutions, catering to the diverse requirements 
of retail, commercial, industrial, aviation, marine and institutional customers across India. Its offerings span 
transportation fuels, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), lubricants, bitumen, aviation turbine fuel, natural gas and 
other value-added energy solutions.
In line with the evolving energy landscape and India’s transition towards a low-carbon economy, HPCL continues to diversify its 
energy portfolio through investments in biofuels, compressed biogas (CBG), liquefied natural gas (LNG), green hydrogen, electric 
mobility infrastructure and renewable energy. Simultaneously, the Company is expanding its nationwide infrastructure, modernising 
refining and marketing assets, and leveraging digital technologies to enhance operational excellence and customer experience.
These strategic initiatives reinforce HPCL’s commitment to delivering safe, reliable, efficient and sustainable energy solutions 
while creating long-term value for stakeholders and contributing to India’s energy security and sustainable development.

Dear Stakeholder(s),
It gives me immense pleasure to present the 74th Annual Report 
of your Company. As I complete my first full year in this esteemed 
Corporation, I am privileged to share HPCL’s performance, 
achievements and strategic progress during FY 2025-26.
Each milestone in this Annual Report tells a story. Every 
number represents collective efforts of our stakeholders whose 
commitment transforms vision into reality. Their dedication, 
perseverance and shared sense of purpose helped serve millions 
of customers across the length and breadth of India.
Our Stakeholder’s commitment to excellence made it possible 
to overcome every challenge and convert every opportunity into 
measurable success. The performance reflected is not merely 
the outcome of financial and operational achievements, but 
represents the spirit of One HPCL. One Purpose. This 74th Annual 
Report is, above all, a tribute to the people and partnerships 
that make this organisation what it is, and it is my privilege to 
share their story.
As India’s GDP continues to grow at a strong rate of 7.7% in 
FY 2025-26, it reinforces its position as the world’s fastest-
growing major economy. The energy sector continued to remain 
one of the major drivers contributing to India’s growth. On the 
global stage, India ranks as the world’s 3rd largest consumer of 
oil and primary energy.
In this backdrop, FY 2025-26 marked another defining chapter 
in HPCL’s distinguished journey, one characterised by strategic 
progress in key initiatives and a steadfast commitment to 
nation-building. ‘Sashakt Bharat’ is not a slogan for us—it is a 
responsibility we carry to work each morning. As India aims for 
its rightful place among the largest economies, energy is the 
current that will carry it there, and HPCL intends to remain a 
reliable partner in that journey.
For over five decades, HPCL has evolved with India’s growth story, 
building a legacy founded on trust, innovation and excellence. As 
one of the country’s leading energy companies with a significant 
presence across refining, marketing and pipeline infrastructure, 
our progress reflects a relentless pursuit of value creation and 
operational leadership.
Today, as we stand on the threshold of a rapidly transforming 
energy landscape, we remain guided by HP FIRST values that 
have shaped our journey. These values continue to underpin 
our commitment to delivering energy responsibly, creating 
enduring stakeholder value and contributing meaningfully to 
India’s development.
Your faith in HPCL inspires us to continually raise our 
aspirations, embrace new opportunities and build a stronger, 
more sustainable future together.
Navigating a Complex Economic 
Environment
The 2025-26 fiscal cycle navigated intense turbulence in the 
global crude oil market, accentuated by a steep price spike 
in March 2026. This led to a shift in trade routes, driven by 
escalating geopolitical friction in West Asia. When supplies 
from the Strait of Hormuz stopped, our supply and operations 
teams worked round the clock so that not a single citizen was 
left waiting at a fuel pump or for supply of cooking gas cylinder. 
Volatility, we have come to learn, is not an interruption to our 
work—it is the very terrain on which we prove our worth.
The operating environment towards the close of the financial 
year was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainties. 
During FY 2025-26, the Company aggressively diversified its 
energy supply chain by integrating 10 new grades into our crude 
basket. This strategic move elevates our total portfolio to a 
formidable 188 crude grades. Spot purchase of LPG during the 
year from outside Gulf countries strengthened diversification 
of otherwise concentrated LPG procurement from a particular 
region.
Specific measures for supply optimisation included nil imports of 
MS/HSD enabled by strategic sourcing from domestic refineries, 
cost takeout initiatives and improved coastal and rail logistics. 
These measures by our different teams boosted both supply 
chain resilience and enhanced logistical efficiency.
The supply chain disruptions were also proactively managed 
through flexible contractual structures and prudent inventory 
management. The integrated sourcing-to-marketing approach 
strongly positioned the company in a dynamic gas market.
As India advances towards its vision of becoming a developed 
economy, the energy sector has an increasingly critical role to 
play. Ensuring energy availability, affordability and sustainability 
will be central to supporting economic progress and improving 
quality of life for millions of citizens.
At HPCL, we remain deeply committed to this national agenda. 
Guided by our purpose of energising lives and enabling progress, 
we continued to strengthen our core businesses, invest in 
future-ready capabilities and create sustainable value for all 
stakeholders.
At the heart of this journey lies 
the trust and confidence of our 
stakeholders. I extend my sincere 
gratitude to our customers,  
shareholders, business partners 
and all stakeholders for their  
continued support.”

Delivering Strong Performance
HPCL reported a record Profit After Tax of ₹17,175 crore. Revenue 
from Operations stood at ₹4,78,543 crore, while EBITDA reached 
₹33,182 crore. The Corporation achieved its highest-ever sales 
volume of 51.45 MMT, each figure is the sum of countless 
decisions taken well, seamless operations conducted on ground 
and the priceless trust our customers place in us every single 
day.
Project Samriddhi (the EBITDA improvement program of the 
corporation) delivered benefits of ₹ 1,691 crore through focused 
interventions in cost optimisation, operational excellence and 
margin enhancement.
We improved our balance sheet strength significantly during the 
year, supported by prudent capital allocation, disciplined cost 
management and a continued focus on operational excellence. 
Net worth stood at ₹59,847 crore as on March 31, 2026, while 
the debt-equity ratio improved to 0.80 from 1.38 as on March 
31, 2025. These achievements underscore our ability to navigate 
market volatility while remaining focused on long-term value 
creation. The improved balance sheet strength provided us the 
muscle to fight the challenges posed by West Asia crisis.
Refining Excellence
Refining continues to be one of HPCL’s strongest pillars of value 
creation. During FY 2025–26, our refineries processed a record 
crude throughput of 26.04 MMT. Capacity utilisation stood at 
106.3%, reflecting sustained operational excellence and efficient 
asset management. Gross Refining Margin for the year stood at 
US$ 8.79 per barrel.
Visakh Refinery clocked its highest-ever annual crude throughput 
of 16.04 MMT (107% capacity utilisation), supported by improved 
reliability and effective use of upgraded process units.
A defining milestone of the year was the commissioning of 
the Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) at Visakh Refinery, 
incorporating the world’s first and largest LC-MAX technology 
installation. For decades, the heavy residue at the bottom of 
the barrel was treated as the limit of what a refinery could 
achieve. As this asset advances through stabilisation towards 
its designed operating performance, this state-of-the-art 
facility will transform an unprecedented 93% of bottom-of-the-
barrel residue, thereby improving product value realisation. It 
has positioned Visakh Refinery as one of the most sophisticated 
refining complexes in the region. It is an asset that reflects 
not only engineering excellence but also HPCL’s confidence in 
investing for the future. The RUF is equipped with DigiSuite, 
which provides real-time process insights and monitors catalyst 
performance and equipment health through advanced data 
analytics.
At Mumbai Refinery, multiple optimisation initiatives contributed 
to improved reliability, higher throughput and enhanced 
profitability. During the year, Mumbai Refinery achieved its 
highest crude throughput of 10 MMT and recorded its lowest-
ever Fuel & Loss of 6.75 wt%.
Advanced Process Control (APC) was commissioned in all units 
of Visakh Refinery Modernisation Project (VRMP). Additionally, 
advanced digital process optimisation techniques including Real 
Time Optimiser (RTO) were commissioned across multiple units 
of Mumbai Refinery (MR) and Visakh Refinery (VR). These key 
digital initiatives will enhance operational efficiency, optimise 
energy utilisation and improve refinery performance.
Our continued investments in technology, digitisation and 
process optimisation will ensure that HPCL’s refining assets 
remain globally competitive and future-ready.
Strengthening Energy Infrastructure
HPCL continues to invest in strategic infrastructure that 
enhances capacity, strengthens supply chains and supports 
future growth.

The HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL) project made 
significant progress during FY 2025–26. Overall physical 
completion reached 91.6%, bringing this transformational project 
to the threshold of commissioning. Subsequent to the close of 
the financial year, the refinery was successfully commissioned, 
marking a defining milestone in HPCL’s growth journey. On 4th 
July 2026, it was Dedicated to the Nation by the Hon’ble Prime 
Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi Ji. This landmark event 
symbolised the culmination of a vision realised through the 
dedication and perseverance of thousands of people over the 
years.
Once fully operational, HRRL will be one of India’s most 
advanced integrated refinery and petrochemical complexes. It 
will significantly strengthen HPCL’s downstream portfolio and 
enhance long-term value creation.
We also continued to invest in pipelines, LPG bottling plants, 
terminals, depots, Biofuels, logistics infrastructure and 
Renewables. During the year, capital expenditure amounted to 
₹15,705 crore was made reflecting our commitment to building 
a future-ready energy ecosystem. These investments will 
strengthen energy accessibility while creating long-term value 
for stakeholders.
Marketing Excellence: Serving a  
Growing Nation
HPCL’s marketing business delivered another year of strong 
performance, supported by expanding demand, customer-
centric initiatives and an extensive distribution network. Total 
sales volume reached a record 51.45 MMT during the year. Retail 
sales stood at 30.83 MMT, while LPG sales reached 9.41 MMT.
Our retail network expanded by 1,351 outlets during the year, 
taking the total network to 25,098 outlets across the country. 
Simultaneously, we strengthened our non-fuel retailing 
initiatives and digital customer engagement platforms. HP 
Gas continued to reinforce its position as one of India’s most 
trusted LPG brands. Our customer base increased by 17.3 lakh 
new connections, supported by a robust distribution network 
comprising 6,389 distributors nationwide.
The Aviation business recorded sales of 1.16 MMT, while the 
Lubricants business achieved sales of 686 TMT. The Industrial 
and Commercial business also delivered strong performance 
through sector-specific solutions and enhanced customer 
engagement. As customer expectations continue to evolve, we 
remain focused on delivering superior experiences, convenience 
and reliability across all business segments.
Building the Gas and Alternate Energy 
Ecosystem
Natural gas is expected to play a critical role in India’s evolving 
energy mix. During FY 2025–26, HPCL strengthened its presence 
across the gas value chain through investments in LNG, City Gas 
Distribution and gas marketing infrastructure.
Our Natural gas portfolio expanded to 624 TMT, while the 
CGD segment recorded total sales (CNG+PNG) of 149 TMT. 
HPCL’s participation across multiple CGD entities continues 
to strengthen our position in India’s growing gas economy. 
Simultaneously, we continued to develop alternate energy 
infrastructure. The number of EV charging stations (including 
Battery Swapping Stations) installed across our retail network 
increased to 5,533 while CNG-enabled outlets reached 2,253 
locations. These initiatives support our vision of becoming 
a diversified energy company capable of meeting evolving 
customer needs. And, when the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India 
dedicated our Chhara LNG Terminal to the nation, it marked 
more than the addition of an asset—it marked HPCL’s arrival in 
the LNG age.

Innovation and Research-Led Growth
During the year, our R&D teams focused on refining technologies, 
process optimisation, sustainability solutions, biofuels and 
emerging energy opportunities. We filed 118 new patents 
during FY 2025–26, bringing the cumulative number of patent 
applications to 779 of which 66 patents were granted, bringing 
the total granted patents to 312.
Your Company continues to foster a culture of innovation by 
collaborating with startups to develop advanced solutions 
across the oil and gas value chain. As of March 31, 2026, 28 
startups have received support, with cumulative disbursements 
of approximately ₹28.6 crore. These initiatives reflect our 
commitment to advancing continuous innovation and 
improvement.
Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, advanced 
analytics, machine learning and predictive maintenance are 
increasingly transforming the way we operate and create value. 
We remain committed to leveraging innovation to improve 
operational efficiency, strengthen sustainability and unlock 
new growth opportunities.
Accelerating Digital Transformation
At HPCL, digital transformation is not merely a technology 
initiative; it is a business transformation programme designed 
to enhance agility, efficiency and customer-centricity. During 
FY 2025–26, we implemented several digital initiatives across 
refining, marketing and corporate functions.
A Digital Transformation Roadmap is in place, with multiple 
projects completed and others ongoing. Advanced analytics 
platforms, enterprise-wide dashboards and automation 
solutions are enabling faster decision-making and improved 
business performance.
Today, every Strategic Business Unit is an active participant 
in HPCL’s digital transformation journey. By democratising the 
digital movement across the organisation, we have embedded 
digital thinking as a shared capability that is driving innovation, 
agility and sustainable growth.
Advancing the Energy Transition
The global transition towards cleaner energy presents both 
opportunities and responsibilities. I am often asked how an 
oil company should think about a cleaner future. My answer 
is simple: not as a threat to be managed, but as a chance to 
be earned. India is already ahead of its global commitments—
and we intend to be among the builders of that future, not 
bystanders to it. At HPCL, we recognise that India’s transition 
pathway must balance the energy security, affordability and 
sustainability.
Accordingly, we are pursuing a diversified approach that 
combines conventional energy leadership with investments in 
emerging energy solutions.
During the year, renewable energy capacity increased to 241 
MW, advancing our pipeline of solar and wind assets. Green 
hydrogen remains a key strategic focus area. During FY 2025–26, 
Green H2 Purchase Agreement (GHPA) was signed with OCIOR 
Green Fuels Pvt Ltd for supply of 5 KTPA to Visakh Refinery 
on a BOO basis. Some of the year’s most quietly remarkable 
work happened at the edges of what we believed is possible: 
at Visakh, we turned used cooking oil—the very kind discarded 
from household kitchens—into sustainable aviation fuel; and in 
our laboratories, we coaxed bio-crude from seaweed. Modest 
steps today, perhaps, but they are the seeds of the energy 
company we are determined to become.
To contribute to India’s energy self-reliance, we achieved 
19.94% ethanol blending rate this year. Additionally, under the 
Government of India’s SATAT initiative to promote Compressed 
Biogas (CBG) as an alternative transport fuel, HPCL added three 
new CBG plants and increased the total CBG Plants under the 
SATAT scheme to 18. These efforts underscore our commitment 
to building a future-ready energy portfolio.
Sustainability at the Core 
Sustainability continues to guide our strategic decisions and 
operational priorities.
During FY 2025–26, HPCL refineries achieved energy savings of 
86,542 SRFT and reduced greenhouse gas emissions by 0.28 
MTCO2e.
HPCL’s focus areas to advance its sustainable development 
agenda include decarbonisation, transition to clean energy, 
improved resource efficiency and responsible governance.
HPCL remains committed to achieving Net Zero emissions by 
2040 and continues to invest in initiatives that support this 
long-term ambition.
People: The Foundation of Our Success
We believe our success is largely fuelled by the dedication 
and commitment of our people. During FY 2025–26, employees 
completed over 74,268 person-days of training through various

capability-building programmes. Leadership development, 
digital upskilling and technical training remained key focus 
areas. We are dedicated to creating a safe, inclusive and 
empowering workplace where employees can thrive and 
contribute meaningfully.
Safety remains our highest priority, with over 11,752 safety 
training person-days delivered through immersive AR/VR 
modules to reinforce safety competencies.
We also launched SAFE 100, a 100-day organisation-wide safety 
drive to accelerate cultural change and reinforce operational 
discipline.
These initiatives reflect our unwavering focus on upskilling, 
safety and operational integrity.
Creating Shared Value
Our commitment to Nation-building extends beyond business 
operations. With CSR initiatives focused on education, 
healthcare, sanitation, women empowerment and skill 
development, we are laying the foundation for meaningful 
and lasting impact on communities. During FY 2025–26, HPCL 
allocated ₹97.05 crore towards CSR initiatives supporting around 
130 activities and projects for local area development in the 
vicinity of its operating locations. One of these stays with me 
above the rest. Under ‘Dil without Bill’, we helped fund heart 
surgeries for children from families who could never have 
afforded them. When you realise that a child is breathing 
easier tonight because of work this Corporation chose to do, 
you understand that nation-building is not merely a phrase in 
a report—it is the purpose that defines our existence.
Looking Ahead
The future presents immense opportunities for HPCL. India’s 
appetite for energy will only grow in the years ahead, and 
with it both our opportunity and our obligation. But I do not 
measure our future merely in barrels or volumes. I measure it 
in our readiness to change while staying true to who we are—a 
Company that keeps the Nation moving, lights its homes and 
working towards a cleaner horizon. The energy landscape will 
be reshaped by technology and by the demands of sustainability 
and your Company intends to help shape it rather than be 
shaped by it.
HPCL is well-positioned to thrive in this environment. Backed 
by strong fundamentals, strategic investments, world-class 
assets, a talented workforce and committed partners, we 
remain confident in our ability to create sustainable value 
while contributing meaningfully to India’s growth journey. Our 
greatest strength is the shared belief, held at every level of this 
Corporation, that our work matters to our Country. As we move 
forward, our commitment remains unwavering, to strengthen 
energy security, accelerate the energy transition, create value 
for stakeholders and support the Nation’s vision of a prosperous, 
self-reliant and sustainable future.
I extend my sincere gratitude to the Ministry of Petroleum & 
Natural Gas, allied Ministries in the Govt of India, State Govts, 
our Board of Directors, Employees, Customers, Shareholders, 
Business Partners and all Stakeholders for their continued trust 
and support.
Together, we will continue to power possibilities and realise the 
dream of a Sashakt Bharat.
Thank you,

Remuneration of Directors
The remuneration of HPCL’s Board-level executives and 
senior management is governed by the guidelines issued by 
the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) for Central Public 
Sector Enterprises (CPSEs). As the nodal authority for CPSEs, the 
DPE prescribes policies relating to remuneration, performance 
evaluation, organisational autonomy, financial delegation and 
human resource management, thereby ensuring consistency, 
transparency and accountability across public sector enterprises.

structured remuneration framework comprising pay scales, 
allowances, performance-related pay, retirement benefits and 
other applicable compensation components for Board-level 
executives and senior management. The remuneration policy

Board of Directors and, wherever required, are submitted to the 
Administrative Ministry for issuance of Presidential Directives.

MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT 
Materiality assessment forms the foundation of HPCL’s sustainability strategy by identifying and prioritising 
the environmental, social and governance (ESG) topics that have the greatest influence on long-term value 
creation, business performance and stakeholder decision-making. It supports effective risk management, strategic 
planning and transparent sustainability reporting.
Setting ESG Priorities for Long-term Value 
During FY 2025–26, HPCL reviewed its material ESG topics, 
building on the previous assessment to ensure continued 
alignment with evolving business priorities, stakeholder 
expectations and global sustainability practices. The review 
included validation of the existing materiality matrix against 
internationally recognised frameworks, including GRI 11 – Oil 
& Gas, SASB and IPIECA, together with benchmarking against 
industry peers and consideration of emerging regulatory 
developments, policy priorities and investor expectations.
Stakeholder perspectives were reaffirmed through 
structured engagement with employees (management 
and non-management), dealers, distributors, suppliers, 
contractors, transporters, customers, local communities, 
vulnerable and marginalised groups, and industry peers, 
ensuring that the assessment continued to reflect the 
expectations of key stakeholder groups.
Based on the review, the materiality matrix remained 
unchanged during FY 2025–26, reaffirming the relevance of 
HPCL’s existing sustainability priorities and their continued 
alignment with the Company’s long-term strategy. To further 
strengthen ESG performance management, HPCL mapped 
defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to each material 
topic, enabling more effective monitoring, performance 
evaluation and integration of sustainability considerations 
into business planning and decision-making across the 
value chain.
48

ESG Priorities for Strategic Impact 
HPCL’s ESG priorities provide the strategic foundation for integrating sustainability across its business operations and long-term 
growth agenda. Developed through a structured four-stage materiality assessment, they reflect the environmental, social and 
governance issues that are most significant to the Company and its stakeholders, while addressing emerging risks, opportunities 
and evolving regulatory and market expectations.

Benchmarking Inputs
HPCL validated its ESG priorities by benchmarking them 
against internationally recognised frameworks, including 
GRI, SASB and IPIECA, alongside peer disclosures and 
leading investor-focused sustainability assessments. This 
exercise helped ensure that the Company’s materiality 
assessment remains aligned with evolving global 
practices, industry trends and stakeholder expectations.
2
Government and Regulatory Inputs
HPCL assessed emerging government policies, 
regulatory developments and sector-specific compliance 
requirements to validate the continued relevance of its 
material ESG topics and ensure alignment with national 
priorities and the evolving regulatory landscape.
3
Stakeholder Survey
HPCL conducted structured stakeholder engagements 
involving employees, dealers, suppliers, transporters, 
business peers and vulnerable communities to validate 
its material ESG topics. Stakeholders evaluated each 
topic based on its significance, likelihood, scale and 
severity of impact, providing valuable inputs to the 
materiality assessment.

Materiality Assessment
Inputs from benchmarking, regulatory reviews and 
stakeholder engagement were synthesised to identify 
and prioritise the ESG topics most material to HPCL.

Macroeconomic Risk
Risk Drivers
Mitigation Measures
HPCL’s core reliance on crude oil imports as primary source 
of raw material exposes it to a spectrum of macroeconomic 
risks. Global crude oil and product price volatility, supply 
chain disruptions, storage constraints and geopolitical 
situations pose significant risks to HPCL’s operations and 
financial position.
• Diversification of Crude oil and LPG sourcing is done 
to minimise concentration risk and maintain supply 
security during geopolitical disruptions.

adequate measures to increase storage capacity 
including strategic storage for Crude and LPG.
• HPCL has a policy framework on Oil Price Risk 
Management (OPRM), approved by its Board. Mitigation 
measures including hedging positions are taken by the 
OPRM Committee from time to time.

Capital Allocation
HPCL continued to pursue a disciplined capital allocation 
strategy during FY 2025–26, balancing growth investments 
with financial prudence to strengthen its core businesses while 
accelerating the transition towards a diversified and future-
ready energy portfolio. During the year, the Company incurred a 
total capital expenditure of ₹15,705 Crore, including investments 
in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates, while maintaining 
a prudent long-term debt-to-equity ratio of 0.60.
Of the total capital expenditure, ₹3,997 Crore was invested in the 
Refining business and ₹7,272 Crore in Marketing and corporate. 
As of 31 March 2026, cumulative investments in subsidiaries 
and joint ventures stood at ₹20,877.59  Crore, reflecting HPCL’s 
long-term commitment to strengthening its integrated energy 
portfolio.
Capital deployment remained focused on expanding refining 
and marketing infrastructure while advancing investments 
in renewable energy, biofuels, natural gas infrastructure and 
alternative energy solutions, supporting the Company’s Net 
Zero by 2040 aspiration and long-term business transformation.
FINANCIAL CAPITAL (Contd.)
Debt Management and Financial Prudence
HPCL maintained a prudent and well-diversified capital structure 
during FY 2025–26, ensuring adequate financial flexibility to 
support business growth, strategic investments and long-term 
value creation. As on 31 March 2026, the Company’s gross debt 
stood at ₹47,598.66 Crore, comprising approximately 36% foreign 
currency borrowings and 64% domestic borrowings, reflecting a 
balanced and diversified funding portfolio. The long-term debt-
to-equity ratio remained at a comfortable 0.60, while the total 
finance cost for the year amounted to ₹3,149.46 Crore.
The Company continued to actively optimise its borrowing 
portfolio through an appropriate mix of domestic and 
international funding, with a well-balanced maturity profile 
aligned to its long-term capital requirements. This disciplined 
approach to debt management supports HPCL’s ongoing 
infrastructure expansion, energy transition investments and 
overall financial resilience.

Refining Infrastructure
HPCL’s refining operations are anchored by two technologically 
advanced refineries located in Mumbai (9.5 MMTPA) and 
Visakhapatnam (15.0 MMTPA), providing the Company with a 
strong manufacturing base to meet the nation’s growing energy 
demand.  Both the refineries produce BS-VI compliant fuels, 
supporting cleaner mobility, while the Mumbai Refinery also 
houses India’s largest lube refinery, with a Lube Oil Base Stock 
(LOBS) production capacity of 428 TMTPA, representing over 
40% of the country’s installed LOBS capacity. 
The Company further strengthens its refining portfolio through 
strategic investments in key downstream joint ventures. HPCL 
holds a 48.993% stake in HPCL-Mittal Energy Limited (HMEL), 
which operates an 11.3 MMTPA refinery at Bathinda, Punjab, 
and a 16.955% stake in Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals 
Limited (MRPL), which has  a refining capacity of 15.0 MMTPA. 
HPCL is also developing the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited 
(HRRL) project at Pachpadra, Barmer, in partnership with the 
Government of Rajasthan, with a 74% equity stake. Progressive 
commissioning of 9 MMTPA integrated grassroot Reﬁnery-
cum-Petrochemical project at Balotra, Rajasthan (HRRL) is in 
progress. Crude is taken in CDU/VDU. This has facilitated the 
commencement of commissioning activities of secondary units 
in a sequential manner. Upon commissioning, HRRL will establish 
India’s first integrated greenfield refinery-cum-petrochemical 
complex, significantly enhancing the Company’s refining and 
petrochemical capabilities while supporting the country’s long-
term energy and industrial growth.

technological leadership.

Technology Commercialisation and Scale-Up
Commercialisation of indigenous technologies is a key pillar of HPCL’s innovation strategy, enabling the Company to transform 
research outcomes into commercially viable solutions that enhance operational excellence, strengthen technological self-
reliance and create long-term business value. By accelerating the deployment of home-grown technologies across refining, 
petrochemicals, clean energy and specialty products, HPCL continues to support the Government of India’s Aatmanirbhar 
Bharat initiative while reinforcing its competitive advantage.
HP-DAK Technology: HPCL successfully commissioned 
the 52 KTPA HP-DAK Plant at its Mumbai Refinery, marking 
the commercial-scale deployment of this indigenously 
developed technology. The plant has demonstrated stable 
and sustained operations, validated the technology’s 
commercial viability while reinforced HPCL’s technological 
self-reliance, and operational excellence.
HP-COSOL: Since its deployment across all three Lube 
Solvent Extraction Units at the Mumbai Refinery in 2022, 
HP-COSOL has consistently delivered stable plant-scale 
performance.
HP-AEME (Green Hydrogen Electrolyser): HPGRDC 
successfully scaled up its proprietary Anion Exchange 
Membrane (AEM) Electrolyser technology to a 1 MW-
equivalent cell size for performance validation and 
demonstration. With manufacturing partners engaged 
to support commercial-scale production, the technology 
is advancing towards deployment and is expected to 
strengthen HPCL’s capabilities in green hydrogen and next-
generation electrolysis technologies.
HP-TDAE (Treated Distillate Aromatic Extract 
Technology): HPCL’s proprietary process for the production 
of environmentally compliant Treated Distillate Aromatic 
Extract (TDAE) rubber processing oils, low in Polycyclic 
Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAH), progressed towards 
commercialisation during FY 2025-26. The 48 KTPA plant at 
the Mumbai Refinery achieved mechanical completion and 
is being readied for commissioning.
HP-NTO (Naphtha-to-Olefins Technology): To accelerate 
the commercialisation of HP-NTO technology, HPCL entered 
into a Joint Development and Cooperation Agreement (JDCA) 
with Lummus Technology, USA.
Product Scale-Up (PSU) Facility: HPGRDC’s dedicated 
Product Scale-Up facility is being used extensively to scale up 
in house developed chemicals and additives from laboratory 
to trial and demonstration volumes. During FY 2025-26, 10 
products were scaled up to a total of approximately 18 MT 
for field trials and demonstrations, accelerating the pathway 
from research to commercial readiness.
HP-PSA: Commercialisation of HPCL’s proprietary HP-
PSA technology gained momentum through a strategic 
collaboration with Engineers India Limited (EIL). While EIL 
is actively pursuing commercial opportunities with potential 
customers, the MR-ROG PSA project at Mumbai Refinery 
is being jointly executed by HPCL and EIL, supporting the 
technology’s large-scale commercial deployment.
HP-BH2 (CO2 Capture Technology):  During FY 2025–26, 
HPCL commissioned a 24 KTPA CO2 capture demonstration 
unit at the Visakh Refinery based on HiGAS (Rotating 
Packed Bed) technology for carbon capture from Hydrogen

Advancing Circular Economy and 
Sustainability through Innovation 
HPCL continues to leverage its research and innovation 
capabilities to develop technologies that promote circular 
economy principles, resource efficiency and the transition 
towards a low-carbon future. Through the HP Green R&D Centre 
(HPGRDC), the Company is advancing innovative solutions that 
convert waste into valuable resources, reduce dependence on 
virgin materials and support the development of sustainable 
fuels and circular products.
Key innovations during FY 2025–26 include
Plastic Pyrolysis Oil (PPO) Co-processing: Successfully 
completed co-processing trials of waste Plastic Pyrolysis Oil 
(PPO) at the Mumbai Refinery's New Fluid Catalytic Cracking 
(NFCC) Unit, demonstrating the conversion of plastic waste into 
transportation fuels and petrochemical feedstocks. 
HP-PCR HDPE: Developed HP-PCR HDPE, a 100% recycled High-
Density Polyethylene (HDPE) formulation using proprietary 
additives for HP lubricant packaging. The product delivers 
performance comparable to conventional lubricant containers 
while significantly reducing the consumption of virgin polymer 
and promoting sustainable packaging solutions.
Used Cooking Oil (UCO) to Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF): HP 
TRIJET, an indigenous process developed by HPGRDC, enables 
conversion of used cooking oil into Sustainable Aviation Fuel 
(SAF), green diesel and green naphtha. The technology has 
been validated at lab and pilot scale, with BDEP completed and 
detailed engineering underway for a 7.4 KTPA demonstration 
unit at Visakh Refinery, supporting low-carbon aviation fuel 
development and waste-to-fuel pathways.
Green Hydrogen Initiatives
Green hydrogen is a strategic pillar of HPCL’s decarbonisation 
roadmap and energy transition strategy. The Company continues 
to invest in indigenous technologies, pilot-scale demonstrations 
and supporting infrastructure to build capabilities across the 
green hydrogen value chain, reinforcing its long-term vision of 
becoming a diversified and low-carbon energy company.
HPCL operates India’s first refinery-based Green Hydrogen 
pilot plant at the Visakh Refinery, with an Alkaline Electrolyser 
capacity of 370 TPA. The facility serves as a technology 
demonstration platform for evaluating the integration of green 
hydrogen into refinery operations and advancing low-carbon 
industrial processes.
To strengthen its technology leadership, the HP Green R&D 
Centre (HPGRDC) is actively pursuing research across multiple 
next-generation electrolysis technologies, including Alkaline, 
Anion Exchange Membrane (AEM), Proton Exchange Membrane 
(PEM) and Solid Oxide Electrolyser (SOE) systems. HPGRDC 
achieved a significant milestone by successfully scaling its 
proprietary AEM Electrolyser technology to a 1 MW-equivalent 
cell size for performance validation and demonstration.
HPCL is also expanding the enabling infrastructure for the 
hydrogen economy. The Company is establishing India’s 
first 700-bar Hydrogen Refuelling Station at Bayyavaram, 
Visakhapatnam, which is expected to be commissioned by the 
end of FY 2026–27. The project will support the adoption of fuel 
cell mobility solutions and contribute to the development of 
India’s emerging hydrogen ecosystem.

Process Safety Management (PSM) remains a cornerstone of 
HPCL's operational excellence, supporting the safe and reliable 
operation of its refining assets through robust risk management, 
governance and continuous performance monitoring.
Across the Company's refineries, process safety risks are 
systematically identified, assessed and managed by designated 
risk champions and process owners. Risk mitigation measures 
and implementation progress are periodically reviewed through 
established governance mechanisms, with regular oversight at 
the Strategic Business Unit (SBU) level and reporting to the 
Board.
To strengthen process safety performance, HPCL continuously 
monitors Tier-3 and Tier-4 leading process safety indicators, 
with monthly reviews undertaken to identify emerging risks, 
drive preventive actions and reinforce continuous improvement 
across refinery operations.

HPCL’s Approach to IFRS S2 Climate-related 
Disclosures
Climate change is a strategic business priority for HPCL and 
is integrated into the Company’s long-term business strategy, 
enterprise risk management framework and investment 
decisions. Recognising the evolving physical and transition risks 
associated with climate change, HPCL continues to strengthen 
its climate resilience while pursuing opportunities arising from 
the transition to a low-carbon economy.
Aligned with its Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040 
ambition, the Company is embedding climate considerations 
across its refining, marketing, logistics, infrastructure 
development and corporate governance processes. HPCL’s 
decarbonisation strategy is driven by initiatives in renewable 
energy, energy efficiency, cleaner fuels, green hydrogen, 
biofuels, carbon management, circular economy practices and 
other low-carbon technologies.
Consistent with the principles of IFRS S2 Climate-related 
Disclosures, HPCL continues to enhance its climate governance, 
climate risk and opportunity assessment, greenhouse gas 
emissions management, scenario analysis and climate-
related performance monitoring. Through these initiatives, the 
Company aims to strengthen business resilience, support India’s 
energy transition and create sustainable long-term value for its 
stakeholders.
Governance
HPCL has established a robust governance framework to 
oversee its sustainability and climate transition agenda, 
ensuring effective Board oversight, executive accountability 
and integration of climate-related considerations into strategic 
decision-making. The Corporate Social Responsibility and 
Sustainable Development (CSR & SD) Committee of the Board, 
comprising Whole-time and Independent Directors and chaired 
by an Independent Director, provides strategic guidance on 
sustainability and climate-related matters. The Committee 
periodically reviews the Company’s progress towards its Net 
Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040 commitment, 
monitors key environmental, social and governance (ESG) 
priorities, and oversees the implementation of sustainability-
related strategies and initiatives.
To accelerate its energy transition, HPCL has also established 
dedicated business verticals for natural gas, biofuels, renewable 
energy and other emerging low-carbon businesses, enabling the 
Company to capture new growth opportunities while advancing its 
decarbonisation objectives. This governance framework promotes 
cross-functional collaboration, strengthens enterprise-wide 
accountability and supports informed decision-making to enhance 
long-term business resilience and sustainable value creation.
Strategy
HPCL’s climate strategy is centred on building a resilient, 
diversified and low-carbon energy portfolio while supporting 
India’s energy transition and strengthening long-term 
shareholder value. Guided by its Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 
emissions by 2040 ambition, the Company is embedding climate 
considerations into its business strategy, investment planning 
and operational decision-making.
The Company’s decarbonisation roadmap is anchored on four 
strategic pillars: transformative energy efficiency, accelerated 
deployment of renewable energy, promotion of biofuels and 
circular economy initiatives, and investment in green hydrogen 
and carbon management technologies. These pillars support 
the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, enhance resource 
efficiency and improve operational resilience across the value 
chain.
HPCL is progressively reducing its Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 
while expanding its presence in cleaner and emerging energy 
businesses. Through investments in renewable energy, natural gas, 
green hydrogen, biofuels, sustainable aviation fuel, e-mobility and 
other low-carbon technologies, the Company is transforming into 
a diversified, future-ready integrated energy enterprise.
The strategy also enables HPCL to address climate-related 
risks, capitalise on emerging business opportunities, diversify 
revenue streams and strengthen the resilience of its portfolio 
in a transitioning, carbon-constrained economy. By balancing 
energy security, affordability and sustainability, HPCL is 
committed to delivering reliable energy solutions while creating 
sustainable long-term value for all stakeholders.

Climate Risk Management
HPCL has established a robust Enterprise Risk Management 
(ERM) Framework to systematically identify, assess, monitor 
and manage climate-related risks and opportunities across 
its operations, projects and business functions. Climate 
considerations are integrated into enterprise risk management, 
strategic planning and investment decision-making, enabling 
the Company to strengthen business resilience, enhance 
adaptive capacity and create sustainable long-term value.
Recognising the evolving energy landscape, HPCL continuously 
evaluates both transition risks arising from the shift towards 
a low-carbon economy and physical risks associated with 
climate change. The Company periodically reviews these risks 
and implements appropriate mitigation measures to safeguard 
its operations, assets and stakeholders.
Key Climate-related Risks
Transition Risks
• Accelerated adoption of cleaner and alternative energy 
solutions may progressively influence long-term demand 
for conventional hydrocarbon fuels.
• Evolving climate-related regulations, carbon pricing 
mechanisms, disclosure requirements and stakeholder 
expectations may impact business operations, investments 
and market competitiveness.
• Increasing expectations regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emissions management, air quality and environmental 
performance necessitate continual improvements in 
operational efficiency and regulatory compliance.
Physical Risks
• Increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather 
events, rising temperatures and water stress may affect 
operational continuity, infrastructure resilience and supply 
chain reliability at certain locations.
Key Mitigation Measures
• Expanding presence across biofuels, renewable energy, CNG 
infrastructure, EV charging and battery swapping networks 
to support the transition towards cleaner energy solutions. 
• Advancing Net Zero goals for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions 
by 2040, supported by dedicated investments towards green 
and low-carbon business initiatives. 
•  Integrating energy efficiency measures across existing 
operations and upcoming projects, while establishing green 
hydrogen facilities at refinery locations. 
•  Strengthening research and innovation efforts focused on 
emerging green technologies, sustainable fuels and carbon 
management solutions.

Nine Locations Achieve Net Zero Operational Carbon Certification
India’s Net Zero ambition for 2070 gives HPCL its horizon; 
the Corporation’s own roadmap to Net Zero for Scope 1 and 
Scope 2 operational carbon by 2040 sets the pace. In FY 2025 
26, the Supply, Operations and Distribution(SOD) SBU turned 
that pledge into a national first.
Through sustained decarbonisation measures and sustainable 
operating practices, SOD SBU achieved Net Zero Operational 
Carbon Certification at nine locations, making HPCL the first 
company in India to certify a Net Zero Operational Facility. 
The milestone was celebrated at the 14th GreenCo Summit 
2025 in Hyderabad, held on the theme “Green Makes Business 
Sense” with the co theme “Beyond Commitments: Scaling 
Net Zero Action for 2030 and Beyond,” in the presence of Shri 
Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Honourable Minister for Information 
Technology, Electronics, Communications, Industries and 
Commerce, Government of Telangana, along with senior 
officials from the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).
HPCL’s Secunderabad Terminal was honoured as India’s first 
location certified as a Net Zero Operational Carbon Location, 
followed by eight more: Miraj IRD, Kolkata Terminal, Sholapur 
IRD, Durgapur IRD, Visakh New White Oil Terminal, Haldia 
Terminal, Ramagundam IRD and Manmad IRD. Reinforcing this 
leadership, 12 SOD locations were awarded GreenCo Platinum 
and Gold Certification for their progress on sustainability.
The recognition was hard earned. The Net Zero certification, 
conducted by CII, followed a rigorous evaluation: a 12 month 
data review, comprehensive physical inspections, and 
assessment across policy and commitment, GHG emission 
inventory, action plans, mitigation strategies, sustenance 
measures and Scope 3 screening. By meeting the standard 
for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, SOD SBU has set a new 
industry benchmark and given HPCL’s 2040 commitment a 
proven, replicable template.

Water Conservation Initiatives
Effluent Treatment and Recycling
HPCL adopts a circular approach to water management by 
maximising the treatment, recycling and reuse of wastewater 
across its operations. The Company has established Effluent 
Treatment Plants (ETPs) and Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) at 
major operational locations to ensure responsible wastewater 
management, minimise freshwater withdrawal and enhance 
water-use efficiency.
At refinery locations, wastewater is treated through physical, 
chemical, biological and tertiary treatment processes to meet 
the prescribed Minimum National Standards (MINAS) before 
being reused for operational purposes such as cooling tower 
make-up, fire water systems, utility services and horticulture. 
Effluent discharges are continuously monitored to ensure 
compliance with applicable environmental regulations and to 
maintain high standards of environmental performance.
During FY 2025–26, HPCL’s refineries and marketing locations 
recycled over 66,833 million kilolitres (KL) of water(including 
Bearing Cooling Water Recirculation), reinforcing the Company’s 
commitment to sustainable water stewardship and resource 
conservation.
Rainwater Harvesting
HPCL continues to strengthen water security through the 
implementation of rainwater harvesting systems across its 
operational locations. These initiatives support groundwater 
recharge, augment local water availability and reduce 
dependence on freshwater sources, particularly in water-
stressed regions.
Water Positivity 
HPCL is committed to strengthening its water stewardship 
practices by progressively transitioning towards water-positive 
operations. Recognising water as a critical natural capital 
resource, the Company aims to minimise freshwater withdrawal, 
maximise water recycling and reuse, and replenish water 
resources through conservation and recharge initiatives across 
its operational footprint.
The Company’s water positivity strategy is built on four 
key pillars:
• Optimising freshwater consumption through process 
improvements, digital monitoring and water-efficient 
technologies.
• Maximising wastewater recycling and reuse by enhancing 
the performance and capacity of Effluent Treatment Plants 
(ETPs) and Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs).
• Replenishing water resources through rainwater harvesting, 
groundwater recharge, watershed development and 
community water conservation projects, particularly in 
water-stressed regions.
• Strengthening water governance through risk assessment, 
water accounting, performance monitoring and stakeholder 
engagement.
Waste Management
HPCL adopts a circular economy-based approach to waste 
management, focusing on waste minimisation, resource recovery 
and responsible disposal across its operations. The Company 
strives to reduce waste generation at source, maximise reuse and 
recycling, and ensure the environmentally sound management of 
hazardous and non-hazardous waste in accordance with applicable 
regulatory requirements and recognised industry best practices.
Through systematic waste segregation, recycling, co-processing 
and recovery initiatives, HPCL continues to improve resource

sustainable operations across its refineries, marketing installations 
and other operational facilities.
Hazardous Wastes
HPCL follows stringent procedures for the identification, handling, 
storage, transportation and disposal of hazardous waste to

chemical residues, spent catalysts, sludge and other hazardous 
wastes are managed in compliance with applicable environmental 
regulations and are disposed of through Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) and Central Pollution 
Control Board (CPCB) authorised treatment, recycling and disposal 
facilities. Continuous monitoring and robust control measures 
ensure environmentally responsible management throughout the 
waste lifecycle.

Metallic scrap generated across HPCL’s operations is recovered 
and recycled through structured resource recovery mechanisms. 
Scrap LPG cylinders, valves, regulators and other metallic 
materials are processed in accordance with established 
Company procedures and disposed of through MSTC to 
authorised recyclers for recycling and material recovery. These 
initiatives promote circular resource utilisation, conserve 
natural resources and reduce waste sent for final disposal.
NATURAL CAPITAL (Contd.)
Biodiversity
HPCL recognises biodiversity and healthy ecosystems as 
essential components of natural capital and is committed to 
conserving and enhancing ecological value across its operational 
footprint. The Company integrates biodiversity considerations 
into its environmental management practices by protecting 
and expanding green spaces, promoting native vegetation and 
supporting ecosystem restoration, wherever feasible.
Across its refineries, marketing installations, terminals, depots, 
pipeline locations and residential townships, HPCL develops and 
maintains green belts comprising native tree species, shrubs, 
herbs and landscaped areas. These green spaces contribute 
to improved environmental quality by enhancing carbon 
sequestration, supporting local biodiversity, reducing dust and 
noise levels, improving microclimatic conditions and providing 
habitats for birds, butterflies and other local fauna.
Biodiversity Conservation
Recognising the importance of biodiversity conservation in 
maintaining healthy ecosystems, HPCL continues to support 
initiatives aimed at protecting endangered wildlife species 
beyond its operational boundaries. As part of this commitment, 
the Corporation continued its association with the Himalayan 
Zoological Park, Sikkim under the “My Child from Wild – Zoo 
Animal Adoption Programme”.
128

During FY 2025-26, HPCL renewed the adoption of three Red 
Pandas supported in previous years and expanded the initiative 
by adopting two additional Red Pandas—Keemo Reep (Male) and 
Songru Pundi (Female)—taking the total number of adopted Red 
Pandas to five. The programme supports the care, nutrition, 
veterinary treatment and habitat management of the adopted 
animals, thereby contributing to the conservation of this 
endangered species.
Through such initiatives, HPCL complements its environmental 
stewardship efforts by supporting biodiversity conservation and 
fostering greater awareness on the protection of wildlife and 
natural ecosystems.
Afforestation and Green Cover  
During FY 2025–26, HPCL continued to strengthen its biodiversity 
conservation initiatives through plantation drives, green belt 
development and urban ecosystem restoration across its 
operational locations.
At the Mumbai Refinery, the Company planted 2,000 saplings 
and continued the maintenance of the Miyawaki Forest at the 
Maharana Pratap Technical Institute, Kurla, supporting urban 
biodiversity, carbon sequestration and the development of 
resilient micro-ecosystems within the refinery neighbourhood.
At the Visakh Refinery, plantation programmes were organised at 
Waltair Park and Yarada Park Housing Colonies on the occasion of 
Hassan Terminal: Lake Spillway Clean Up under 
Swachhata Hi Sewa
As part of the Swachhata Hi Sewa campaign, HPCL Hassan 
turned intent into action at Satyamangala Lake, the city’s 
largest and best loved waterbody. In just two hours, the 
terminal’s dedicated team cleared a full truckload of waste 
from the lake’s spillway, transforming a polluted channel 
into clean, free flowing water. It was a small window of 
effort with a lasting result, reinforcing HPCL’s commitment 
to Swachh Bharat and to a greener, healthier future for the 
communities it serves.

8. Approval of Material Related Party 
Transactions with HPCL-Mittal Energy 
Limited
HPCL-Mittal Energy Limited (“HMEL”) is a Related Party 
as defined under Section 2(76) of the Companies Act, 2013 
(“Act”) read with Regulation 2 (1) (zb) of the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015 (“SEBI LODR, 2015”).
The Company is proposing to enter into certain business 
transactions with HMEL during Financial Year 2027-28. The 
nature of transactions include purchase/sale of goods 
(such as, Petroleum/Petrochemical products, Crude etc.), 
availment/providing of services, lease rental etc. from/
to HMEL, and receipt of dividend. All transactions to 
be entered into by the Company with HMEL are in the 
ordinary course of business and are at arm’s length basis 
and necessary approvals as required in compliance of the 
provisions under the Act/ SEBI LODR, 2015 were obtained 
from the Audit Committee/Board.
It may be noted that as per the explanation to Regulation 
23 (1) of SEBI LODR, 2015, a transaction with a related 
party shall be considered material if the transaction(s) 
to be entered into individually or taken together with 
previous transactions during a Financial Year, exceeds 
₹3,000 Crore plus 2.5% of the annual consolidated 
turnover of the listed entity above ₹40,000 Crore or ₹5,000 
Crore, whichever is lower. Further, all Material Related 
Party Transactions require prior approval of the Members 
through a Resolution and no related party shall vote to 
approve such resolution whether an entity is a related 
party to the particular transaction or not.
The transactions with HMEL for Financial Year 2027-28 
are estimated to be ₹ 1,46,000 Crore (Rupees One Lakh 
Forty Six Thousand Crore Only) and this amount exceeds 
above-mentioned threshold limit and therefore it is a 
Material Related Party Transaction. Accordingly, it requires 
prior approval of the Company by way of passing of an 
Ordinary Resolution.
Approval of the Members of the Company is therefore 
required in terms of Regulation 23 of the SEBI LODR, 2015 
by way of passing of an Ordinary Resolution for approval 
to the aforesaid Material Related Party Transactions to be 
entered for Financial Year 2027-28.
The Members at the 73rd AGM held on August 22, 2025, had 
granted approval for entering into Material Related Party 
Transactions with HMEL for up to ₹91,000 Crore during 
FY 2026-27. As a matter of abundant caution, the approval 
of the Members is sought for continuation of the said 
Material Related Party Transactions from the conclusion 
of the 74th AGM i.e. from August 26, 2026 till March 31, 2027, 
in line with the amendments to Regulation 23(4) of SEBI 
LODR, 2015, effective December 19, 2025.
Relevant documents, if any, in respect of the said item are 
available in electronic form for inspection by the Members 
of the Company upto the date of AGM.
The Directors, Key Managerial Personnel or their relatives 
holding shares of the Company may be deemed to be 
concerned or otherwise interested in the said Ordinary 
Resolution only to the extent of their shareholding.
The Board recommends the Ordinary Resolution as set out 
for approval by the Members.

Directors’ Report
DEAR MEMBERS,
On behalf of the Board of Directors, it gives me immense pleasure in presenting this Report on the performance of your Corporation 
for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
Financial Year 2025 - 26 has been a year of strong operational and marketing performance with stellar profitability of ₹ 17,175 
Crore. The resilient refinery operations, sustained growth in market sales, healthy refining margins and continued progress in 
improving the company’s financial strengths, were hallmark achievements of your Corporation for the year.  In this series, your 
Corporation achieved highest-ever refinery throughput of 26.04 million metric tonne (MMT) with an annual growth of 3.0%, and 
also the highest ever sales of 51.45 MMT, reflecting an impressive growth of 3.3% over the previous year.
The close of the year witnessed conflicts arising in Middle East leading to supply uncertainties and resultant volatility in the 
prices of Crude Oil and Petroleum Products in the international markets, and associated implications in the domestic market. 
These geopolitical developments are bound to have a pronounced impact on the Corporation, in the near future.

Refinery Performance
The financial year 2025–26 stands as a landmark year for HPCL 
Refineries, marked by exceptional operational and physical 
performance. Driven by a combination of proactive planning, 
technology-enabled optimization and agile decision-making, 
your Corporation achieved its highest-ever crude throughput 
of 26.04 MMT, surpassing the previous record of 25.27 MMT 
achieved in financial year 2024–25. This achievement was 
further reinforced by robust crude planning and agile supply 
chain management during the geopolitical disruptions in 
March 2026, enabling seamless operations and maximization 
of refinery throughput.
The Visakh Refinery delivered an outstanding performance 
by processing its highest-ever annual crude throughput of 
16.04 MMT (107% capacity utilization), supported by enhanced 
reliability and effective utilization of upgraded process units. 
The Mumbai Refinery also demonstrated strong operational 
excellence, achieving a highest ever annual crude throughput 
of 10.00 MMT (105% capacity utilization), with sustained focus 
on efficiency, reliability, and optimization.
Strong operational performance and optimization initiatives 
led to record production of MS, HSD, LPG alongside achieving 
the distillate yield of 75.8 wt% during the year. Visakh Refinery 
achieved highest ever ATF production of 252 TMT. Mumbai 
Refinery also achieved its lowest ever Fuel & Loss of 6.75 wt% 
during the year.
The Refineries ability to adapt became exceptionally strong as 
we embraced new opportunity crudes and processed 10 new 
grades of crude for the first time. This surpassed the 8 numbers 
of new crude grades processed during financial year 2024-25. 
Further during the financial year 2025-26, 10 new grades were 
added to the Company’s crude basket, which now includes 188 
grades from various regions such as West Africa, Middle East, 
North America, South America, Mediterranean, North Sea, Far 
East, Russia and India.
India’s energy demand is set to grow, driven by its rapid economic 
growth. The rising demand for road transport fuels further adds 
to this increasing trend. Part of this increased demand is met 
by modernization and expansion of our refineries.
Your Corporation has successfully commissioned the Residue 
Upgradation Facility (RUF) at its Visakh Refinery during 
December 2025, featuring the world’s first and largest LC-Max 
unit—a major leap in advanced refining. With a capacity of 3.55 
MMTPA, this LC-Max–based RUF is among the world’s most 
advanced facilities, enabling 93% conversion of bottom-of-the-
barrel residues into high-value distillates. The unit enhances 
the refinery’s ability to process heavier and opportunity 
crudes while improving product quality and overall operational 
efficiency. RUF was provided with “DigiSuite” to have real time 
process insights, catalyst and critical equipment condition 
using data analytics.
Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project is being 
taken up in Mumbai Refinery to increase the LOBS Production 
from current 475 KTPA to 764 KTPA and increase in Bitumen 
Production by approx. 487 KTPA, is progressing at good pace 
and has achieved significant milestones during the year.

Official Language Implementation
Being a PSE, certain constitutional provisions and provisions 
of Official Language Act 1963, Official Language Rules 1976 
and Presidential Guidelines w.r.t. Official Languages are 
applicable to your Corporation. The Official Language (OL) 
Implementation Report of the Company is submitted to the 
Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas on quarterly basis.
OL implementation is ensured in the official communications 
of the Corporation by motivating the employees through 
persuasion, motivation and incentives. Hindi is being 
promoted by utilizing various facilities available in the field 
of Information & Technology. To promote the linguistic talent 
of the employees, awareness about Hindi is created in the 
offices through on-line Hindi Competitions, Hindi Fortnights, 
Official Language Conferences and Hindi Workshops etc. Team 
Rajbhasha ensures timely Hindi translations of the company’s 
annual report, SBU’s procedural literatures and other important 
documents. National festivals and other important programs 
are anchored in Hindi by Rajbhasha officers.
Periodical inspections of HPCL offices are carried out by 
representatives of the Committee of Parliament on Official 
Language, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Petroleum 
and Natural Gas. In these inspections, HPCL’s official language 
performance is always appreciated and HPCL is referred to as 
a model company for other organizations.
HPCL is coordinating Town Official Language Implementation 
Committee (TOLIC) of Mumbai based PSUs since 1983. Our 
C&MD is the chairman of Mumbai PSU TOLIC and presides 
half yearly meetings of the committee. Other than the TOLIC 
Meetings, HPCL conducts various programs to train and guide 
the officials of member PSUs throughout the year.
HPCL was conferred with Prestigious ‘Rajbhasha Keerti 
Puraskar’ for the year 2024-25 by Ministry of Home Affairs. 
This award is given for the best performance in the field of OLI 
amongst all PSUs. HPCL has maintained its record in entire Oil 
Industry by receiving 54 Rajbhasha Awards from Government 
of India and other agencies during the year 2025-26.

Procurement Of Goods & Services From 
MSEs
The Government of India has notified a Public Procurement 
Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 2012, and its 
amendments thereto. In line with said policy, your Corporation 
has set an annual goal of sourcing a minimum procurement of 
25% of its total requirements from MSEs, and within it, 4% of 
the total requirement has been earmarked for procurement 
from MSEs owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs and another 3% 
from women entrepreneurs. For the benefit of MSEs, the MSE 
procurement details are regularly uploaded on the Sambandh 
Portal of the Ministry of MSME, besides displaying the Annual 
Procurement Plan on the Corporation’s website.
The centralized procurement department of your corporation is 
ISO 9001:2015 Certified & also conform to ISO 20400:2017. Your 
organization also prioritizes the implementation of government 
policies aimed at strengthening the MSME ecosystem and 
promoting indigenization, developmental orders, and start-
up orders.
Against the set target of 25% of the total procurement for 
financial year 2025-26, your Corporation has achieved 59.42% 
(₹ 6,679 Crore) of procurement of goods and services from MSEs, 
excluding items that are beyond the scope of MSEs. Also, your 
Corporation has also surpassed the procurement from MSE SC/
ST & MSE Women by Achieving 5.10% (₹ 573 Crore) from MSE SC/
ST and 4.30% (₹ 484 Crore) from MSE Women against the target 
of 4% & 3% respectively. The excluded items are crude oil, 
petroleum products, logistics costs through shipping, railways 
and pipelines, LNG/Natural Gas, API line pipes, OEM spares, OEM 
services, proprietary items and services, technology licenses 
and licensor-mandated items, and plants and machinery (single 
item value equal to or more than ₹ 100 Crore).
To promote the objectives of procurement from MSEs as 
laid down in Public Procurement Policy, Organized 25 vendor 
meets in collaboration with National SC/ST Hub (NSSH), 
attended by 426 vendors, focused on promoting MSE SC/ST 
vendor onboarding, Participation in 8 numbers of National 
Vendor Development Programs (NVDP) arranged by MoMSME 
and 103 nos of Inhouse Vendor meets were organized by CPO 
for training the vendor on procurement process, resolving of 
issues and guiding them on policies. During these meetings, 
the Corporation procurement processes were articulated 
through detailed presentations to MSE vendors with the intent 
of increasing awareness on vendor registration processes, 
tendering processes, the TReDS platform, procurement on the 
GeM platform, etc. The implementation of various government 
directives/policies for providing relief to MSMEs and promoting 
the indigenization of products and services was also explained 
during the programme.
Your Corporation is registered with the TReDS Digital platform, 
an institutional mechanism set up by the Reserve Bank of India 
to facilitate the trade receivable financing of Micro Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) from corporate buyers through 
multiple financiers. Integrating its ERP system with Five of 
the service providers, namely A.Treds Ltd., Mynd Solutions Pvt. 
Ltd., Receivables Exchange of India Ltd. C2 TReDS platform and 
DTX (KredX Platform Pvt Limited, the Corporation has enabled 
MSMEs to auction their trade receivables at competitive rates 
through online bidding by financiers. Numerous MSME vendors 
have onboarded this platform and benefited from the bill 
discounting facility that provides liquidity.

Research and Development
Hindustan Petroleum Green Research & Development Centre 
(HPGRDC) was set up with the objective of developing solutions 
for existing and new business areas. Today, HPGRDC stands not 
just as an R&D Centre for the Refineries but as a beacon of 
excellence across the diverse spectrum of our industry. From 
Refining to Marketing, from Lubes to LPG, and from energy 
transition initiatives to ground-breaking technologies, its 
footprint spans far and wide, leaving an enduring legacy of 
innovation and creativity.
In the pursuit of excellence, during financial year 2025-26, 
HPGRDC signed 8 MoUs for collaborative innovation and 
business development with various national and international 
organizations/institutes during the year. These collaborations, 
undertaken with the clear objective of becoming solution 
providers, signify our commitment to fostering synergistic 
relationships and value creation across the industry.
In addition to our collaborative endeavours and technological 
advancements, we achieved a significant patent milestone of 
779 patent filings and received 312 patent grants. In financial 
year 2025-26, HPGRDC filed 118 patents, taking the cumulative 
Pollution Control Measures initiated and other environment initiatives undertaken by Refineries during

Indian and International patent applications to 779. During 
the year, 66 patents were granted to HPGRDC, taking the 
cumulative patents granted to 312. This solidifies HPGRDC 
position as one of the fastest growing research institute in 
intellectual property creation and innovation.
HPCL remains steadfast in its commitment to indigenization, 
harnessing homegrown talent and expertise to develop 
technologies and products with significant impact. Last year, 
our focus on indigenous solutions led to the development 
of ground-breaking technologies and products that not only 
showcased our technical prowess but also made substantial 
contributions to our operations and the industry at large.
HPGRDC continued innovation with the objective of developing 
solutions for existing and new business areas, with the special 
focus on green chemistry principles. HPGRDC successfully 
developed and 18 Nos. new products catering to refinery 
solutions, corrosion solutions, lube formulations etc. were 
handed over to various strategic business units, showcasing 
immense market potential.
HPCL’s commitment to innovation led to scale-up of R&D 
developed catalysts to commercial scale for utilization in 
refineries. Some of which include HGU PDS Catalyst, HP 
DAK Catalyst (Catalyst for DAK technology), HP DHT (Diesel 
Hydrotreating) catalyst, HP NHT (Naphtha Hydrotreating) 
catalyst, HP AMT (Advanced Matrix Technology FCC catalyst).
Global Technology Centre (GTC) of HPGRDC has undertaken 
various innovative initiatives to improve processes, increase 
operational efficiencies and reduce energy consumption of 
HPCL Refineries. Technical solutions were provided on issues 
such as increasing feed rate in VR HGU PDS, resolving NSU 
pressure drop fluctuation issue, processing off-spec (colour) 
DAO in SEU-III and PDU, achieving on-spec BS production with 
~₹ 6 Crore profit.
Also, as part of its continuous commitment towards net-zero & 
green hydrogen initiatives, HPGRDC is working on development 
of advanced Alkaline-AEM electrolyser technology through 
an integrated approach combining electrode materials 
development, stack engineering and system optimization. 
Currently, this is being scaled up to 1 MW scale. The salient 
features include higher hydrogen purity from AEM stack, low 
severity operation and comparatively less power consumption.
Furthermore, HPCL has made significant strides in battery 
technology development, exemplified by our in-house 
innovations in lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries. The 
lithium-ion cylindrical cell, featuring inhouse Lithium Nickel 
Manganese Oxide cathode and graphite anode, has achieved 
impressive energy density. Additionally, beyond Lithium-
ion initiatives, ground breaking work on development of 
cathode materials for Sodium ion batteries have resulted in 
successful development of high-voltage cathode materials, 
such as Sodium Vanadium Fluorophosphate and layered 
oxide cathode materials. These have culminated in the scale 
up of cathode material and demonstration of sodium-ion 
batteries, showcasing our commitment to diversifying energy 
storage solutions.

Corporate Governance Report
Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (“Company/HPCL”) 
is a Government Company and a ‘Maharatna’ Central Public 
Sector Enterprise (“CPSE”) listed on BSE Limited (“BSE”) and 
National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”) and governed 
by SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR, 2015”) and Guidelines on 
Corporate Governance (“DPE Guidelines”) issued by Department 
of Public Enterprises (“DPE”).
As required under Schedule V of SEBI LODR, 2015, disclosure 
relating to “Related Party” and “Management Discussion and 
Analysis” have been dealt with in other parts of this Integrated 
Annual Report while the Corporate Governance Report is 
appended below.
Philosophy on Corporate Governance
At HPCL, Corporate Governance is to meet the Stakeholders 
aspirations and Societal expectations. The key principles on 
which this edifice is built includes well developed internal 
controls, systems and processes, transparency in business 
operations, performance and financial position, clearly defined 
management performance & accountability and full adherence 
to compliances and disclosures.
This is made possible due to its well-defined Policy framework 
which includes Code of Conduct for Directors and Senior 
Management Personnel, Integrity Pact to enhance transparency 
in business operations, Public Grievance Redressal Mechanism, 
Whistleblower Policy, Empowerment and Authority Manual and 
the Procurement Manual.
Being a Government Company, its activities are reviewed by 
several external authorities like the Comptroller & Auditor 
General of India (“C&AG”), the Central Vigilance Commission 
(“CVC”), Parliamentary Committees etc. The Annual Report on 
the affairs and working of the Company along with comments of 
C&AG is also placed regularly in both the Houses of Parliament.
Structure of Corporate Governance in HPCL
At the apex level of the structure is the Board which has 
constituted several sub-committees viz. Audit Committee, 
Risk Management Committee, Nomination & Remuneration 
Committee, Stakeholders Relationship Committee, CSR and 
Sustainability Development Committee and Project Evaluation 
and Review Committee, the composition of which and the 
meetings held during the Financial Year 2025-26 are separately 
covered in this Report and summarised below:

6. Right to Information Act, 2005:
	
HPCL being a Public Authority is under the statutory 
obligation to comply with the provisions of the Right to 
Information Act, 2005 and therefore has a structured 
mechanism in place to deal with matters related to the RTI 
Act, and has also aligned to the Online RTI portal of DoPT, 
Government of India. All RTI applications/ first appeals 
received through the portal are handled through the portal 
itself, including the physical applications received offline. 
The mandatory reports such as Quarterly/ Annual reports 
are submitted periodically within the stipulated timelines 
on to the website of the Central Information Commission 
https://cic.gov.in/ . Further, as required under the said Act, 
all the relevant details and information mandated vide 
suo-motu disclosures under Section 4 (1) (b) are being 
regularly updated and hosted on the company’s corporate 
website www.hindustanpetroleum.com for the purpose 
of transparency and better understanding to the public 
at large.
	
HPCL has a designated Nodal Officer at its Corporate HQO 
to coordinate, facilitate and oversee its implementation. 
RTI applications are responded well within the stipulated 
time period of 30 days through the Online RTI portal 
www.rtionline.gov.in. The current team of 216 Nos Central 
Public Information Officers (Regional Managers and HoDs
